**7B.2 Research Note: Lula da Silva in 2024**

Overall: **mixed, leaning negative on correction/accountability.** I found some evidence that Lula’s government corrected misinformation and maintained some transparency, but on politically costly claims he often doubled down, blamed others, or tolerated coercive information tactics. I found **no strong direct evidence** that Lula himself was punished for truth-telling by courts or legislature; the clearest negative signals are instead rhetorical doubling-down, market-sensitive spin, and pressure on the information environment.

**Accepted claims**

- **Title:** Lula denies interference with Federal Police and judiciary  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-01-30  
  **URL:** https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/01/30/lula-rebate-acusacoes-de-bolsonaro-sobre-operacao-da-pf.amp.htm  
  **Summary:** Lula said his government does not interfere with the Federal Police or the judiciary and that the PF operation followed court orders. This is positive evidence that he publicly defended institutional process rather than denying inconvenient facts.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Brazil to mark anniversary of January 8 attack on democracy  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 2024-01-08  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/brazil-to-mark-anniversary-of-january-8-attack-on-democracy-3269163  
  **Summary:** Lula treated the January 8 coup attempt as real and called for punishment of the perpetrators. That supports a truth-telling posture on a major domestic threat rather than denial or minimization.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Lula says he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Blinken  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-02-21  
  **URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm  
  **Summary:** Lula and Planalto publicly presented his position as peace-oriented and anti-war. This is a positive example of consistent messaging to a foreign partner, not evident deception.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Brazil and China sign peace proposal for Ukraine war  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-05-23  
  **URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm  
  **Summary:** The joint statement emphasized dialogue, negotiation, and a ceasefire. This is another sign of public, stable messaging rather than concealment or opportunistic contradiction.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** YouTube removes false claims about Lula’s health  
  **Publisher:** Advocacia-Geral da União  
  **Date:** 2024-12-16  
  **URL:** https://www.gov.br/agu/pt-br/comunicacao/noticias/youtube-retira-do-ar-desinformacao-sobre-estado-de-saude-do-presidente-da-republica  
  **Summary:** The government acted against viral false claims about Lula’s death or serious decline, which is evidence of correcting falsehoods rather than exploiting them. This is the clearest pro-correction item I found, though it is about misinformation control more than self-criticism.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Brazil will not retract Lula’s Gaza comments  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 2024-02-20  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/brazil-will-not-retract-lulas-gaza-comments-in-diplomatic-row-with-israel-sources/1972033/  
  **Summary:** Reuters reported that Brazil would not retract Lula’s Holocaust/Gaza comparison after the diplomatic blowback. This is strong negative evidence: rather than correcting a controversial claim, Lula’s camp stood by it.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Lula repeats genocide accusation against Israel  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-02-23  
  **URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm  
  **Summary:** Lula doubled down on the genocide accusation after the row had already started. This is the clearest counterexample to admitting error or correcting a false or overstated claim.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Lula renews central bank criticism  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-07-01  
  **URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/07/01/lula-critica-bc-autonomo-e-diz-que-autoridade-monetaria-nao-atende-populacao.htm  
  **Summary:** Lula pressed the central bank to “look at Brazil” rather than market preferences, and Reuters said the remarks were worsening market pricing. This is negative evidence for correction: he appears to have prioritized political framing over acknowledging credibility costs.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** TCU prosecutor seeks probe into Petrobras interference  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL  
  **Date:** 2024-03-18  
  **URL:** https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/03/18/ministerio-publico-do-tcu-pede-investigacao-de-possivel-interferencia-do-governo-na-petrobras.htm  
  **Summary:** The TCU prosecutor said the dividend decision looked driven by government preferences rather than economics. This is indirect counterevidence: Lula’s side appears to have presented a politically motivated move as something else.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** Brazil struggles with misinformation and platform pressure  
  **Publisher:** Reuters Institute  
  **Date:** 2024-06-17  
  **URL:** https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/brazil  
  **Summary:** The report says the fake-news bill would have shifted responsibility onto platforms, and the justice minister threatened hourly fines when Google opposed it. This suggests a willingness to pressure the information environment rather than simply tolerate truthful reporting.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

- **Title:** X blocked in Brazil after refusal to obey legal orders  
  **Publisher:** Reuters Institute  
  **Date:** 2024-09-16  
  **URL:** https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/x-has-been-blocked-brazil-does-it-matter-journalism  
  **Summary:** The report describes a tighter online environment, with journalists split over whether the block was lawful enforcement or speech restriction. This is cautionary evidence that truthful reporting online faced real pressure, even if Lula was not clearly the direct actor.  
  **Question IDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1

**Search gap**
- I found **little direct evidence** about Lula admitting errors to the legislature or courts in 2024.
- I also found **no clear case** of Lula personally punishing an identifiable truth-teller for telling the truth.
- The strongest negative evidence is instead **doubling down on the Gaza comparison**, **pressuring the central bank**, and **supporting tighter information controls**.
